Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 8 for the Special Town Meeting warrant.
Proposed the threshold increase to eliminate assessment overhead on accounts with minimal tax yield.

plastic-bag-ban-bylaw.name: Plastic bag ban citizen petition
plastic-bag-ban-bylaw.description: Citizen petition bylaw proposal to ban single-use plastic bags in Southborough commercial establishments.
plastic-bag-ban-bylaw.status: The Advisory Committee voted 0-7 to recommend disapproval of Article 34, a citizen petition to ban non-reusable plastic checkout bags, citing concerns that it was drafted as an unenforceable advisory measure ahead of Annual Town Meeting.

police-drone-program.name: Police Department drone program
police-drone-program.description: Proposed acquisition of a five-year police drone program package funded through unspent municipal personnel funds.
police-drone-program.status: The town has authorized the acquisition of a five-year police drone program, with the Municipal Technology Committee most recently recommending conditional approval for phased deployment. The Select Board voted to fund the $105,000 contract using surplus department personnel funds, offset by external contributions from Fay School and a state earmark. Implementation is moving forward under a pilot framework requiring pre-deployment verification and formal reviews after 90 days and 12 months.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 27 to recommend conditional approval and phased deployment with formal reviews after 90 days and 12 months.
Approved the $105,000 purchase 3-2 on June 29 using surplus personnel funds, balancing immediate public safety needs against concerns about bypassing Town Meeting.
Voted 3-0 on June 24 to back the drone program as an immediate capital safety priority, deferring the year-end funding mechanism to the Select Board.

preschool-tuition-and-assistance.name: Public preschool tuition and financial assistance
preschool-tuition-and-assistance.description: Setting annual tuition rates and income-based financial assistance policies for Southborough public preschool programs.
preschool-tuition-and-assistance.status: The School Committee unanimously approved a 3 percent tuition increase for the district preschool program and adopted updated financial assistance guidelines capping fee relief at 10 percent of program revenue.

presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.name: Presidential and Fisher Road waterline looping
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.description: MWRA loan funding and construction to connect dead-end water mains under CSX railroad tracks along Presidential Drive and Fisher Road.
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.status: The waterline looping project along Presidential Drive and Fisher Road is moving forward after the Select Board unanimously approved a $1 million interest-free loan application to the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority in August 2026. Previously authorized by Town Meeting, the project will connect dead-end water mains beneath the CSX railroad tracks to improve water pressure and reduce bacterial buildup. The zero-interest financing is estimated to save the town more than $400,000 in interest costs compared to conventional borrowing.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on August 11, 2026, to authorize the $1 million zero-interest MWRA loan application.

rescinding-unissued-borrowing.name: Rescission of unissued borrowing authorizations
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting warrant article to rescind unused borrowing authorizations for completed capital projects, including Breakneck Hill and the Neary School study.
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.status: Article 6 is headed to Special Town Meeting to rescind over $1.1 million in unissued borrowing authority for the completed Neary School feasibility study ($375,000) and Breakneck Hill Farm dump remediation ($727,960). Both the Select Board and Advisory Committee support the article as routine administrative housekeeping to clear town books and prevent future debt. However, the Conservation Commission has requested that the Select Board reduce the Breakneck Hill rescission by $100,000 to preserve borrowing capacity for habitat restoration work.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 6.
Voted 7-0 on Sep 16 to recommend approval, clarifying that the rescission clears town books without affecting available cash.
Voted 4-1 on Sep 17 to ask the Select Board to reduce the Breakneck Hill rescission by $100,000 to retain borrowing capacity for restoration.
Asked to preserve $100,000 of borrowing capacity for Breakneck Hill restoration work; the Conservation Commission granted the request and petitioned the Select Board.

reserve-fund-transfer-policy.name: Reserve Fund transfer policy
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.description: Advisory Committee policy setting standard procedures, executive board oversight, and statutory criteria for departmental Reserve Fund transfer requests.
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.status: The Advisory Committee is updating its Reserve Fund transfer guidelines to establish formal procedures and statutory criteria for departmental requests. Under the draft policy, requests must be vetted by the town administrator and relevant executive boards, shared with the Capital Improvement Planning Committee for capital items, and limited to future, unforeseen expenses rather than retroactive reimbursements. Revisions were incorporated into a clean working draft in August awaiting final committee approval.

positions.detail: Drafting updated transfer guidelines to enforce statutory criteria, require prior administrative review, and prohibit retroactive reimbursements.

route-9-495-gateway-study.name: Route 9 and I-495 gateway corridor study
route-9-495-gateway-study.description: A joint $150,000 planning and infrastructure study with Westborough evaluating economic development, zoning, and infrastructure along the Route 9 and I-495 corridor.
route-9-495-gateway-study.status: A joint application with Westborough for a state Community One Stop for Growth grant to fund the $165,000 corridor study is currently awaiting a decision from the state. The Select Board, Planning Board, and Wastewater Study Committee all support the initiative, which would examine regional wastewater infrastructure, zoning, and economic development along Route 9. If the $150,000 state grant is awarded, Southborough and Westborough would each contribute a $7,500 local match to fund the engineering and planning work.

positions.detail: Helped prepare the joint application and is pausing consultant hiring and full meetings until grant awards are announced.
Voted 4-0 on May 21 to endorse the grant application after adjusting the support letter to protect residential buffers and emphasize commercial tax base growth.
Voted 5-0 on May 19 to approve an amended letter supporting the regional grant application.

route-9-495-gateway-study.next: State announcement of Community One Stop for Growth grant awards in October 2026

route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.name: Route 9 wastewater infrastructure plan
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.description: Planning, site evaluation, and District Improvement Financing for wastewater collection and treatment along the Route 9 corridor.
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.status: Planning for an estimated $40 million to $50 million municipal wastewater system along Route 9 remains under review, with current efforts focused on modular facility design, site identification, and environmental permitting. The Wastewater Study Committee deferred a planned District Improvement Financing warrant article from the fall 2026 Special Town Meeting to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting to allow time for more detailed engineering and financial data. Major hurdles include securing 15 to 20 acres for ground discharge and resolving state Department of Environmental Protection restrictions regarding watershed protection zones.

positions.detail: Supports developing a modular Route 9 collection and treatment system, but postponed bringing financing articles forward until spring 2027 to develop firmer cost estimates.
Voted 4-1 on June 16 to reallocate $30,000 for a District Improvement Financing study, following a 4-0-1 vote in April to extend the wastewater committee's charge through June 2027.

ruby-estates-subdivision.name: Ruby Estates subdivision
ruby-estates-subdivision.description: Six-lot residential subdivision along Lampson Drive off Mount Vickery Road.
ruby-estates-subdivision.status: All six lots in the Ruby Estates subdivision off Mount Vickery Road have been released from covenant following Planning Board approval of a surety agreement in June 2026. Developer Bartolini Builders secured the remaining subdivision improvements with a bond exceeding $324,000 after completing utility installation and the roadway binder course for Lampson Drive. No further municipal board actions are pending.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to accept the surety agreement and release all six lots from the subdivision covenant.

rural-cemetery-water-tower.name: Rural Cemetery stone water tower restoration
rural-cemetery-water-tower.description: Proposed structural evaluation, restoration, and Community Preservation Act funding for the historic stone water tower in Rural Cemetery.
rural-cemetery-water-tower.status: The proposed Community Preservation Act application to assess and restore the historic Rural Cemetery stone water tower is deferred to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting to allow time for consultant documentation and bid specifications. The Historical Commission is pursuing funding for structural evaluation, historic standards, and a long-term maintenance plan. Earlier concepts to convert the interior of the tower into a columbarium have been dropped.

positions.detail: Is moving forward with an application for architectural and engineering assessment and restoration bid specifications.
Agreed in August 2026 to defer review of the project to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting cycle.

salary-administration-plan-amendments.name: Salary Administration Plan amendments
salary-administration-plan-amendments.description: Proposed warrant articles to amend the non-union Salary Administration Plan bylaw, salary grids, and stipend schedules.
salary-administration-plan-amendments.status: The Personnel Board voted 4-0 and the Select Board voted 5-0 to support Article 4 for the Annual Town Meeting warrant, amending the non-union salary grid, acting department head pay, and cemetery agent stipends.

sarsenstone-way-coc.name: Sarsenstone Way Certificate of Compliance
sarsenstone-way-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and archival records search for the 1970s Sarsenstone Way subdivision under DEP file 290-100.
sarsenstone-way-coc.status: The Conservation Commission resolved the matter on August 27, 2026, by unanimously approving a full Certificate of Compliance for the Sarsenstone Way subdivision. The decision followed staff locating historic public works as-built plans verifying that all road and drainage requirements were met. With the order closed, no further board action is required.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on August 27, 2026, to issue a full Certificate of Compliance after historic town records verified compliance with subdivision requirements.

scenic-road-tree-removals.name: DPW scenic road tree removals
scenic-road-tree-removals.description: Tree Warden and DPW hearings and approvals to trim or remove public shade trees along designated scenic roads.
scenic-road-tree-removals.status: The Planning Board and Tree Warden approved the DPW's request to remove four trees and trim one tree along designated scenic roads in April 2026 due to decay and safety hazards. During the hearing, questions were raised regarding tree removal priorities near private wells and the status of replacement plantings owed by utility companies. No further hearings or actions are currently scheduled on this application.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on April 27, 2026, to approve the removal of four trees and the trimming of one tree along scenic roads.
Inquiries focused on prioritizing hazard removals along streets reliant on private wells and obtaining owed replacement tree plantings from utilities.

school-bus-transportation-operations.name: School bus transportation and technology
school-bus-transportation-operations.description: Bus operations, safety tracking technologies, and vendor performance oversight with contractor NRT.
school-bus-transportation-operations.status: School bus operations under contractor NRT have stabilized, with turn-by-turn GPS and live security cameras operational across the district fleet. Implementation of student RFID tap cards remains delayed, leading district administration to pursue contractual penalty deductions against the vendor. The Southborough School Committee received an informational update on these operations in May 2026 without taking formal action, and no further public proceedings are currently scheduled.

school-choice-participation.name: Interdistrict school choice participation
school-choice-participation.description: Annual School Committee evaluation and hearing on whether to participate in the Massachusetts interdistrict school choice program.
school-choice-participation.status: The Southborough School Committee voted unanimously to opt out of the state interdistrict school choice program for the upcoming school year following a public hearing.

school-food-service-contract.name: School food service contract renewal
school-food-service-contract.description: Contract administration, financial performance, and annual renewals for district food services with Whitsons Culinary Group.
school-food-service-contract.status: The School Committee has extended the district's food services contract with Whitsons Culinary Group for the 2026–2027 school year. The renewal incorporates a 3.9% CPI adjustment and maintains a guaranteed return provision following an operational deficit of nearly $59,000 largely driven by shifted health insurance costs. School administration is set to review Whitsons' performance in December to determine whether to continue the contract for a third year or put it out to bid.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 13, 2026, to extend the contract for the 2026–2027 school year.

school-food-service-contract.next: Administration review of contract performance in December 2026

senior-tax-work-off-policy.name: Senior Tax Work-Off policy and slot allocation
senior-tax-work-off-policy.description: Eligibility regulations and position allocations for Southborough's Senior Tax Work-Off property tax abatement program.
senior-tax-work-off-policy.status: The Senior Tax Work-Off policy is approved and in effect following unanimous Select Board action in September 2026. The latest amendments require CORI background checks for participants and exclude them from other employee benefits, building on an April 2026 update that expanded the program from 30 to 40 positions. No further revisions or board actions are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 2, 2026, to re-approve the policy with CORI check requirements and benefit exclusions, having previously expanded the program to 40 slots.

southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.name: Southborough Golf Club Audubon management plan
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.description: Consultant RFP and environmental management plan to achieve Audubon International certification for the Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.status: The Golf Committee voted in October 2026 to commit up to $4,500 from its revolving fund and pay $500 in overdue membership dues to advance Audubon International certification for the Southborough Golf Club. The move covers a funding shortfall after a single consultant proposal from Conservation Works came in at $18,400, exceeding the town's remaining 2018 Community Preservation Act grant. The committee intends to negotiate the final contract scope to establish the environmental management framework ahead of planned work on the golf course irrigation project.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Oct 13 to authorize up to $4,500 from its revolving fund to bridge the consultant funding gap and pay $500 in membership dues.
Residents questioned past attempts at certification and criticized the project's eight-year delay since initial funding, calling for clear milestones.

southborough-golf-club-irrigation.name: Southborough Golf Club irrigation replacement
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.description: Planning, value engineering, and Community Preservation Act funding for replacing the irrigation system at Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.status: The proposal to fund a $1.09 million replacement of the Southborough Golf Club irrigation system heads to Special Town Meeting on October 17, 2026 as Article 3. The article extends a prior $550,000 Community Preservation Act (CPA) grant, requests roughly $434,000 in new CPA funds, and draws $100,000 from the Golf Course Revolving Fund. Town boards are divided: the Select Board, Community Preservation Committee, and Golf Committee support the measure, while the Advisory Committee opposes it on grounds that golf course improvements should be funded through user fees rather than CPA funds. The Golf Committee decided against offering any fallback floor amendments and will present the funding article as written.

positions.detail: Advocating for Article 3 as written at Special Town Meeting without seeking floor amendments.
Voted 4-1 on September 14 to recommend $433,546 in additional CPA funding subject to conservation and certification conditions.
Voted 5-0 on September 24 to recommend approval of Article 3.
Voted 0-7 against Article 3, maintaining the golf course should be self-funded and player surcharges should back borrowing instead of CPA dollars.
Reached consensus on August 27 supporting the design, confirming the proposed pump station and directional boring comply with the conservation restriction.

sta-unit-c-contract.name: Southborough Teachers Association Unit C contract
sta-unit-c-contract.description: Three-year collective bargaining agreement between the Southborough School Committee and the Southborough Teachers Association covering Unit C support staff.
sta-unit-c-contract.status: The three-year collective bargaining agreement covering Unit C administrative assistants and educational support professionals has been approved by the Southborough School Committee. District administration described the contract negotiations as collaborative and productive. The finalized document will be made public once ratified by both parties.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 18, 2026, to approve the three-year agreement covering administrative assistants and educational support professionals.

stewardship-committee-structure.name: Stewardship Committee structure and merger proposal
stewardship-committee-structure.description: Deliberation over committee appointments and a proposal to merge the Stewardship Committee with the Open Space Preservation Commission.
stewardship-committee-structure.status: The Select Board resolved an immediate committee vacancy in August 2026 by amending the Southborough Stewardship Committee's charge to create a fourth at-large seat and appointing Freddie Gillespie. However, the board left open the possibility of a broader future review to consolidate town open space and conservation bodies. Both the Stewardship Committee and the Conservation Commission strongly oppose merging Stewardship with the Open Space Preservation Commission, arguing Stewardship must remain independent to focus on land maintenance. No further merger proposals or structural reviews are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 in August to amend the committee charge to an at-large seat and appointed Gillespie 5-0, while discussing broader future reviews of conservation committee roles.
Opposes merging with the Open Space Preservation Commission, arguing it should remain a distinct entity focused strictly on maintaining Breakneck Hill and the Town Forest.
Voted 5-0 on June 25 to send a letter opposing consolidation of Stewardship with Open Space and supporting the preservation of Stewardship's independent mission.
Residents and the Stewardship chair praised Freddie Gillespie's habitat management record and urged the town to preserve experienced volunteer leadership on land management committees.

stormwater-enterprise-fund.name: Stormwater enterprise fund
stormwater-enterprise-fund.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article to establish a municipal enterprise fund for stormwater management accounting and future funding.
stormwater-enterprise-fund.status: Article 5, which would establish a municipal stormwater enterprise fund beginning in fiscal year 2028, is awaiting Special Town Meeting with endorsements from both town boards. The proposal creates only an accounting framework under state law and does not implement fees or an operating budget. If approved, the structure is intended to eventually allocate stormwater costs based on impervious surface area across commercial, tax-exempt, and residential properties, though any future fee schedule requires separate Town Meeting authorization.

positions.detail: Voted 7-0 on September 16 to recommend approval, emphasizing in its report language that Article 5 creates only an accounting mechanism and sets no fees.
Voted 4-1 on September 15 to recommend approval after reviewing cost models that would shift a portion of stormwater expenses to commercial and tax-exempt parcels.

street-tree-planting-program.name: Street tree planting pilot study
street-tree-planting-program.description: A pilot study and planting program to evaluate street canopy cover and identify replacement tree planting locations.
street-tree-planting-program.status: The Planning Board approved a $5,500 pilot study with Davey Resource Group in June 2026 to assess street tree canopy cover and identify replacement planting sites. The study will review 10 to 15 streets starting from the town center to locate approximately 25 viable sites for new trees. A board member was designated to coordinate with the tree warden on long-term planning, and no subsequent public updates have been scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to approve spending $5,500 from the tree fund for the pilot study proposal.

subdivision-rules-and-regulations-update.name: Subdivision Rules and Regulations review
subdivision-rules-and-regulations-update.description: Comprehensive review and modernization of Southborough's subdivision rules, regulations, and ANR procedures by the Planning Board.
subdivision-rules-and-regulations-update.status: Drafting remains ongoing by the town planner on an Approval Not Required checklist and updated subdivision regulations to establish standardized application guidelines.

tax-payment-agreements-bylaw.name: Delinquent tax payment agreement bylaw
tax-payment-agreements-bylaw.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article accepting state statute to authorize formal payment agreements for delinquent property taxes.
tax-payment-agreements-bylaw.status: The Select Board voted 5-0 to support Article 29 on the Annual Town Meeting warrant authorizing the treasurer to execute formal payment agreements for delinquent property taxes.

town-budget-process-policy.name: Town budget process policy
town-budget-process-policy.description: Draft municipal policy formalizing timelines, board responsibilities, and procedures for constructing the annual town omnibus budget.
town-budget-process-policy.status: The draft budget process policy is currently tabled while the town seeks guidance from Town Counsel and the Department of Revenue on statutory versus advisory committee roles. The Select Board and the Advisory Committee have debated their respective responsibilities, with Advisory insisting that any policy protect its independent authority to evaluate, present, and defend the omnibus budget at Town Meeting rather than requiring consensus. Further action is on hold pending advice from state officials and legal counsel.

positions.detail: Tabled the policy on Sep 15 to consult Town Counsel and the Department of Revenue regarding statutory versus advisory committee responsibilities.
Wants the draft amended to preserve its independent statutory authority to recommend and defend the budget at Town Meeting, while noting the draft currently omits school spending.

town-common-fence-restoration.name: Town Common fence restoration
town-common-fence-restoration.description: Repair and restoration of the historic fence and railings at the Town Common funded by the Community Preservation Act.
town-common-fence-restoration.status: The Select Board awarded the base restoration contract to Kneeland Construction to repair and restore the existing Town Common fence using Community Preservation Act funds. Total base project costs are estimated at $82,000 to $83,000, including engineering and construction oversight. The town is seeking funding from MassDOT or planning a separate bid to replace a section of fence lost during a state highway project.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on June 2 to award the base repair bid to Kneeland Construction.

town-forest-footbridge.name: Town Forest Eagle Scout footbridge
town-forest-footbridge.description: Construction materials, permitting, and approvals for an Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest.
town-forest-footbridge.status: The Stewardship Committee approved the use of pre-cut pressure-treated lumber for the Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest. The decision resolved questions about whether to substitute cedar near a vernal pool and wetland crossing after reviewing research on minimal copper leaching. No further board reviews or upcoming actions are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 4 to authorize using the pre-cut treated lumber, citing Conservation Commission findings on minimal environmental risk.

town-governance-study.name: Town governance structure study
town-governance-study.description: A consultant-led study evaluating Southborough's municipal government structure, town manager authority, and committee organization.
town-governance-study.status: An 18-week study evaluating Southborough's municipal government structure is under review following an initial consultant presentation on October 6. The study by Capital Strategic Strategies is examining town manager authority, committee organization across the town's 68 committees, and potential transitions between charter and bylaw governance models. The Select Board approved the $24,650 contract in August in a 4-1 vote, with one member dissenting over expenditures during projected budget deficits. The process is slated to continue with listening sessions involving town officials and the public.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on Aug 11 to fund the $24,650 study, though one member opposed spending ahead of expected budget deficits.

town-satisfaction-survey.name: 2026 Town Satisfaction Survey
town-satisfaction-survey.description: Design, public outreach, and execution of the townwide resident satisfaction survey conducted by the Municipal Technology Committee.
town-satisfaction-survey.status: The 2026 Southborough Satisfaction Survey is currently underway, running from October 1 through November 30. The Municipal Technology Committee streamlined and shortened this year's questions to improve completion rates following drop-offs in 2025, while adding new sections on senior services and affordable housing. The Affordable Housing Trust contributed revisions to the housing questions, and the Select Board endorsed a framework to address department service findings.

positions.detail: Redesigned and launched the survey to run through November 30, shortening question matrices to improve completion rates and adding questions on housing and senior services.
Reviewed and submitted refined housing questions for the survey, advising clearer terminology for workforce housing and focusing questions on the downtown area.
Endorsed the committee's 90-day action plan on September 2 to address resident feedback on municipal services from the previous survey.

town-website-redesign.name: Town website redesign
town-website-redesign.description: Redesign of the municipal website with vendor CivicPlus and consolidation of standalone departmental pages.
town-website-redesign.status: The planned overhaul of the municipal website with vendor CivicPlus is in preparation, with implementation targeted for early 2027. The Municipal Technology Committee is guiding the effort but has raised concerns that the town lacks dedicated communications personnel to ensure consistent outward messaging. Contract and module negotiations with CivicPlus are slated to begin in November.

positions.detail: Supports the redesign and upcoming CivicPlus module discussions while emphasizing the need for dedicated communications expertise to manage content.

town-website-redesign.next: Contract and module discussions with CivicPlus begin in November 2026.

transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.name: Transfer station fees and regulations
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.description: Department of Public Works updates to transfer station sticker pricing, outside hauling costs, and operational rules for disposal.
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.status: The Select Board has approved fiscal year 2027 transfer station sticker rates and finalized updated operational regulations, including revised Swap Shop rules. The town also voted to continue participating in a 35-community municipal consortium to negotiate bulk pricing for its next refuse disposal contract ahead of a December 2027 expiration. The board will review and execute Southborough's individual contract terms once consortium negotiations are complete.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 2 to remain in the regional waste disposal consortium, following unanimous approval of updated facility regulations in August.

tricentennial-firefighters-muster.name: 2027 Tricentennial Firefighter's Muster
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.description: Organization of a regional firefighter's muster and antique hand tub demonstration at Woodward School in July 2027.
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.status: Planning for the 2027 Tricentennial antique firefighter's muster is underway with an approved budget of $25,000. Eight regional hand tub teams have confirmed participation out of an expected 16 to 20, and catering and live entertainment have been booked. Organizers are currently restoring Southborough's two historic hand tubs and are preparing site and parking layouts for review.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on June 10, 2026, to approve a budget up to $25,000 and is actively reviewing event logistics.

tricentennial-first-day.name: First Day 2027 celebration
tricentennial-first-day.description: Planning for Southborough's January 1, 2027 Tricentennial kickoff celebration featuring family activities, a drone show, and a bonfire.
tricentennial-first-day.status: Planning is moving forward for the January 1, 2027 Tricentennial kickoff celebration, with a contract executed for a 200-drone aerial light show launching from the St. Mark's School field. Logistical details for other activities remain under review, as turf and wiring concerns at Woodward School may shift the bonfire to Finn School or a later date, and the committee is evaluating tractor-pulled wagons after horse-drawn hayride quotes exceeded $5,000. Working group members and staff will inspect potential bonfire sites ahead of finalizing event arrangements at the committee's November meeting.

positions.detail: Executed the contract for the 200-drone light show and is coordinating event logistics, student design contests, and alternative locations for the bonfire.

tricentennial-first-day.next: Site walk to evaluate bonfire locations on October 18, 2026.

tricentennial-glosobo-winter-lights.name: GloSoBo Tricentennial light festival
tricentennial-glosobo-winter-lights.description: Planning, funding, and programming for the GloSoBo winter light celebration scheduled as part of the 2027 Tricentennial.
tricentennial-glosobo-winter-lights.status: The Tricentennial Committee voted 5-0 to officially add the GloSoBo winter celebration of light to the town anniversary calendar, scheduled for December 3, 2027.

tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.name: 2027 Tricentennial Heritage Day Parade
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.description: Planning for an expanded Heritage Day Parade in October 2027 featuring marching units, community floats, and a historic cannon.
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.status: Planning is underway for an expanded 2027 Tricentennial Heritage Day Parade. The Tricentennial Committee is considering adjustments including a 1:00 PM Sunday kickoff to accommodate church services, shifting the de-staging area to Common and St. Mark streets, and adding reenactment battles and artillery firing. Parade organizers will next coordinate route and staging proposals with public safety officials.

positions.detail: Supports an expanded 2027 parade and is evaluating staging, timing, and attraction options to boost spectator attendance.

tricentennial-street-banners.name: Tricentennial commemorative street banners
tricentennial-street-banners.description: Permitting and installation of celebratory banners on utility poles across Southborough's historic villages.
tricentennial-street-banners.status: Following Town Meeting approval of a temporary sign bylaw amendment, town staff and the Tricentennial Committee are finalizing paperwork to secure utility attachment permits for celebratory banners. The committee voted on October 14 to cap the installation at 50 utility poles to avoid incurring utility inspection fees. Staff are completing insurance and application materials for review and approval by National Grid and Verizon.

positions.detail: Voted to finalize a list capped at 50 utility poles to avoid inspection fees while staff completes required utility applications.
Discussed the proposed 50-banner village display in June and directed town administration to coordinate pole permits with utilities.

tricentennial-summer-nights.name: Summer Nights 2027 music festival
tricentennial-summer-nights.description: Expansion of the annual Summer Nights community event into a multi-act music festival for the 2027 Tricentennial.
tricentennial-summer-nights.status: Plans to expand the annual Summer Nights into a full-day music festival on August 21, 2027, are under active development by the Tricentennial Committee. Organizers are finalizing an agreement with a headliner act and researching property parcel boundaries to determine whether a beer garden can be permitted adjacent to Neary School grounds. The working group is preparing to file an accessibility grant and will meet with town administration and public safety officials to confirm staging, layout, and permits.

positions.detail: Organizers are advancing plans for the expanded August 21, 2027 festival featuring multiple stages, food trucks, fireworks, and accessibility shuttles.

tricentennial-summer-nights.next: Accessibility grant application deadline on October 18, 2026

tricentennial-time-capsule.name: Tricentennial time capsule
tricentennial-time-capsule.description: Selection, preservation, and public placement of a commemorative time capsule for Southborough's 300th anniversary.
tricentennial-time-capsule.status: The Tricentennial Committee is moving forward with plans for a 2-foot cube commemorative time capsule designated for indoor storage at the Harvard Depository to avoid water damage. Working groups are preparing formal invitations to local civic organizations, clubs, and schools to submit historical artifacts and archival-grade photo prints. Boy Scout Troop 1 has volunteered to help coordinate item collection.

positions.detail: Supports an archival-grade capsule stored indoors at the Harvard Depository and is preparing to solicit submissions from local organizations.

trottier-finn-expansion-studies.name: Trottier and Finn expansion feasibility studies
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting articles to study expanding Trottier and Finn schools to reconfigure grade levels and take Neary School offline.
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.status: Proposed Special Town Meeting articles seeking up to $500,000 and $324,000 to study expanding Trottier and Finn schools and decommission Neary School face strong municipal opposition. Both the School Committee and the Select Board voted to recommend defeating Articles 2 and 3, citing space analysis showing grade reconfigurations would require sizable building additions to prevent cuts to educational programming. No future meetings or next steps are scheduled in the record.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously to recommend defeating Articles 2 and 3, citing space study findings that grade reconfigurations would require major building additions to prevent severe programming cuts.
Voted 4-1 to recommend that Special Town Meeting defeat Articles 2 and 3.
A resident asked whether the town would have to conduct all three studies if Articles 1, 2, and 3 all pass, and whether study scope covers site capacity for future additions.

trottier-school-roof-replacement.name: Trottier Middle School roof replacement
trottier-school-roof-replacement.description: Proposed funding and MSBA grant reimbursement to replace the roof at Trottier Middle School.
trottier-school-roof-replacement.status: The proposed Trottier Middle School roof replacement is included in the school district's FY27 capital plan, with an estimated gross cost of just under $8.9 million. The project anticipates a Massachusetts School Building Authority grant covering roughly 41% of the total, leaving an estimated net cost to taxpayers of about $5.4 million. Town Meeting voters will be asked to authorize the full gross amount following an anticipated MSBA board decision.

positions.detail: Supports the project as part of the FY27 capital plan and voted 4-0 on March 24, 2026, to approve an informational flyer outlining gross and net costs for voters.

two-family-zoning-amendment.name: Two-family dwelling zoning amendment
two-family-zoning-amendment.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment for Town Meeting to eliminate the requirement that a single-family dwelling exist for two years before converting to a two-family home.
two-family-zoning-amendment.status: Article 2, which would eliminate the two-year waiting period to convert single-family homes into two-family dwellings and allow new two-family construction by special permit, heads to Special Town Meeting. The Zoning Board of Appeals and Select Board both recommend approval, but the Advisory Committee voted against it over concerns about speculative house-flipping, septic capacity, and density. The Planning Board has not yet taken a position as members examine whether the draft language could inadvertently permit two-family homes on smaller commercial lots. The Planning Board will conclude its public hearing on the morning of October 17, 2026, immediately ahead of the Special Town Meeting vote.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Oct 7 to move forward with the warrant article as drafted after declining to make last-minute revisions.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 24 to support Article 2 as revised for the Special Town Meeting warrant.
Voted 3-4 against recommending the article, citing concerns over property flipping, septic capacity, and density in Residential B districts.
Continued its hearing without taking a position, weighing concerns that the draft could unintentionally allow two-family homes on undersized commercial lots.
A former Planning Board chair cautioned that repeating minimum lot size rules across sections creates ambiguity that could affect smaller commercial parcels.

two-family-zoning-amendment.next: Planning Board continued public hearing on October 17, 2026 at 9:05 AM.

well-and-septic-regulations.name: Well and septic regulation amendments
well-and-septic-regulations.description: Board of Health regulations governing private well testing, swimming pool setbacks, and subsurface sewage disposal systems.
well-and-septic-regulations.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved amendments to Southborough's private well and septic regulations in July 2026 following a public hearing. The new rules require separation of roles between septic engineers and installers, ensure physical access for septic repairs, establish a 25-foot well setback from swimming pools, and require well testing prior to real estate transfers unless mutually waived. With the revised regulations enacted, no further board action or hearings are scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on July 7, 2026, to approve the updated well and septic regulations.

youth-services-flagg-school-relocation.name: Youth and Family Services Flagg School relocation
youth-services-flagg-school-relocation.description: Office relocation, fit-out, and furniture funding for the Department of Youth and Family Services move to the Flagg School.
youth-services-flagg-school-relocation.status: The Southborough Youth Commission voted unanimously to allocate up to $5,000 from its donation account for fire-retardant furniture to outfit new department offices at Flagg School ahead of a July 1 move.
